title: Scheduler telemetry bridge and lightweight kernel advisor for prefetch/pipeline decisions
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Problem statement:
The serving runtime currently exposes NVTX ranges and individual kernel metrics, but we lack a reliable, low-overhead mapping between scheduler-level events (request enqueue/handoff, prefill vs decode windows, batch composition) and the per-kernel cost attribution for a given request. That makes it hard to:
- Explain tail latency spikes by linking them to kernel choices or attention path heuristics
- Drive automated kernel-advisor logic that would pick quantized/attention-optimized kernels per-request class
- Surface cross-request interactions (KV cache reuse, prefix amortization) in console heatmaps

Goal:
Build a "scheduler telemetry bridge": a lightweight instrumentation layer + sampling policy that correlates scheduler events with NVTX spans and per-kernel micrometrics to produce request-level kernel attribution signals suitable for dashboards and an internal Kernel Advisor (a heuristic service that suggests better kernel variants and prefetch/batching strategies). The bridge must add <1% overall p99 latency overhead under production sampling and be toggleable per-deployment.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Runtime telemetry bridge component (C++) that:
   - Emits compact fingerprint tags for a request at scheduler handoff points (enqueue, prefill-start, prefill-end, decode-start, decode-end). Fingerprint is 64-bit (hash of route+model-version+slot-seed) to avoid exposing PII.
   - Attaches NVTX ranges and kernel IDs with the fingerprint in sampled traces and to the metrics exporter for aggregation.
   - Collects per-kernel micro-histograms (latency, token-count, concurrency) keyed by fingerprint and phase-tag (PREFILL/DECODE/POSTPROCESS).
2) Adaptive sampling and reservoir policies (Rust/Go module in control plane):
   - Global default sample rate 0.5% of requests, higher for routes flagged as "investigate".
   - Reservoir for heavy requests (tokens>1024) to ensure better coverage.
3) Kernel Advisor prototype (Python service):
   - Periodically queries aggregated attributions and emits suggestions: switch kernel Kx->Ky for route R when Ky reduces median token-cost by >15% without increasing median latency beyond 3%.
   - Stores suggestions as short-lived annotations surfaced in Console rollouts UI.
4) Observability: dashboards + alerting
   - Per-route kernel-attribution heatmap (stacked by phase) for last 7d.
   - Tail-latency attribution panel: show top-3 kernel IDs contributing to 95-99.9 pcts.
   - Data retention: rolling 30d aggregated; raw sampled traces 7d.
5) Tests & rollout plan:
   - Unit and e2e tests for fingerprint propagation and micro-histogram accuracy (synthetic replay harness).
   - Canary rollout to internal infra followed by gradual rollout to 10% of production routes after 2 days stability.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end tracing shows scheduler handoff -> NVTX ranges -> kernel IDs -> aggregated attribution for a sampled request.
- Console displays per-route kernel attribution heatmap for two pilot routes.
- Kernel Advisor issues at least one actionable suggestion during pilot and the suggestion evaluation shows estimated token-cost delta.
- Performance overhead measured as <1% p99 increase at 0.5% sampling in stress tests.

Implementation notes / trade-offs considered:
- Option A: attach full request IDs to spans (easy correlation) — rejected due to sensitive data leakage/privacy.
- Option B: sample at high rate and attach lightweight 64-bit fingerprints — chosen for privacy and low overhead.
- NVTX naming: keep human-readable short tags for local dev but map to numerical IDs in prod telemetry to reduce payload size.
- Aggregation: prefer push-based periodic aggregation of micro-histograms vs high-cardinality metrics to avoid metric explosion.

Instrumentation toggles and config:
- runtime flag: --telemetry-bridge=(off|sampled|always)
- sample-rate config: decimal in control plane with per-route override
- kernel-advisor: feature-flagged in Console and control plane, suggestions require PM approval to apply

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: sampling misses rare pathological cases — mitigate by reservoir policy and manual "investigate" tagging.
- Risk: GPU-side timing noise inflates attribution — mitigate by per-kernel calibration step in test harness and use of median/percentile robust stats.
- Risk: observability cost growth — mitigate by retention/aggregation defaults and whitelist of routes.

Related artifacts and links:
- Design spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RT/Telemetry+Bridge+Design
- Synthetic replay harness (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/replay-harness/pull/412
- Console mockups (Drive): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1-example-console-mockups
- Prototype Kernel Advisor notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/kernel-advisor/blob/main/notebooks/proto.ipynb

Next steps:
- ENG: spike (2d) to implement fingerprint propagation and narrow NVTX naming schema. Marcus will own the spike.
- ENG: implement runtime bridge core (Liam) — split into two PRs: trace propagation + micro-histogram exporter.
- PM: coordinate pilot routes and Slack channel for noisy signals (Priya).
